description: The record's id, unique within its entity in a bundle. Keep the source system's number where it is unique (RFI-014); otherwise mint a stable one
The project the record belongs to. Every entity marked project_scoped carries it
Where the record came from: system, record id, method and confidence. See the source fields below
Codes that place the record in a classification system: MasterFormat, UniFormat, OmniClass, Uniclass, cost code, CSI division
Source fields with no home in the schema, kept under their source names. Never put a schema field here
The system the record was read from: procore, autodesk_build, sage_300, quickbooks_online, csv, pdf, manual
The record's own id in that system. Lets anyone trace a value back to where it came from
How it was read. document means extracted from a PDF or image; model means a machine-learning model produced it; derived means computed from other records
0 to 1. Required when method is document or model, so a reader can tell a typed value from a guessed one
The document the values were extracted from
The code as the system writes it: 09 91 23, B2010, 23-13 11 00, Pr_20_93, 09-100
0 to 1, when a model or rule assigned the code rather than a person
The job number people type. Links the project to the accounting system's job
Owner contract value at award before change orders
Default retainage percentage the owner holds
The party's role on the work
The trade, for a subcontractor or supplier: drywall, electrical, mechanical
The company a person works for, or the parent of a subsidiary
Contact email. Leave out when the bundle is shared outside the company
What kind of document it is
Sheet or document number: A-201, S-103
Where the file lives. A path or a link the reader can open
Hash of the file. Proves which version a value was read from
MasterFormat number as written in the specification: 09 21 16
Section title. Optional because logs often cite the number alone
The specification document the section is in
RFI number as on the log and in correspondence. Never renumber
One line that makes sense in a log listing
Our proposed interpretation so the answer can be a confirmation
Answered means a response was received; closed means it has been acted on
Why that date: the activity or order it holds up
Expected cost of the answer when the platform records one
Expected schedule impact in days when the platform records one
Specification sections the question is about
Submittal number. Resubmittals keep the number and raise the revision
Date the review is due under the contract
Date the reviewed submittal came back
Date the item is needed on site
The specification section the submittal answers
The subcontract or purchase order that buys what is submitted
The submitted package and the returned review
Change event or potential change order number
Date of the event or instruction
Latest date for written notice under the contract
Current estimate of time impact in days
RFIs whose answers gave rise to it
Site observations that gave rise to it
Owner change orders move the contract; commitment change orders move a subcontract or purchase order
Only approved change orders count toward contract value and committed cost
Value of the change. Negative for a deduct
Contract time added. Negative to remove time
The change events this order prices and agrees
Budget lines the change is budgeted to
Void commitments are excluded from committed cost
Value at execution before change orders
Retainage percentage withheld from the vendor
Cost code of the line, as the accounting system numbers it. Its MasterFormat or CSI division goes in classifications
Approved budget changes to date. Kept apart from the original so the history survives
Budget changes submitted but not approved
Cost still expected to finish the line
Change order the cost was incurred under
Budget line the cost draws on
The invoice or timesheet behind the cost
Retainage withheld from the vendor on this line. A release is negative
Whether the cost is billable to the owner
A progress pay application or a plain invoice
Draft billings are excluded from billed to date
End of the period a pay application covers
Work completed and stored materials billed in this period
Amount billed by this document before retainage
Retainage the owner holds on it
Retainage the owner releases on it
Still owed on it. Absent means fully open
Change orders billed for the first time on it
The activity id in the scheduling tool
Remaining or original duration in working days
On the critical path in the latest schedule
Activities that must finish first (finish to start). Other relationship types go in extra
Cost code the activity's work is budgeted to
Work in place by area and trade
Workers on site across all trades
Anything that stopped or slowed work and why
Inspections and tests held and their results
Incidents, near misses and toolbox talks
What was seen. issue is a generic issue from a platform's issue log
Whether a person or a model raised it. A model's observation carries source.confidence
The activity under way when it was seen
Photos or video frames showing it
What is wrong and what fixes it
Ready for review means the trade says it is fixed
The asset's name as tagged: AHU-01, Pump P-3
The kind of asset: air handling unit, pump, door closer
Space or area it serves or sits in
The specification section it was bought under
The subcontract or purchase order that supplied it
